change.title: pr-36882-flat
change.description: Add rolling-updates feature flag and compatibility framework
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Operator guide says the Operator fails without `rolling-updates`, but no Operator code checks the feature
findings.body: The new caution says the Operator "will fail" if `rolling-updates` is not enabled. Nothing under `operator/src/main` mentions `rolling-updates` or `ROLLING_UPDATES`. The upgrade logic picks `RecreateOnImageChangeUpgradeLogic` or `AlwaysRecreateUpgradeLogic` (`operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/upgrade/UpgradeLogicFactory.java:38-41`) without looking at features, and `features.enabled` is only passed through as the `--features` server option (`KeycloakDistConfigurator.java:122-124`). The PR's own `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment` deploys without the feature when the strategy is unset (`UpgradeTest.java:105-106`), and the test still expects the upgrade to work. Either reword the caution to describe what actually needs the feature (the `update-compatibility` commands inside the server image), or add the Operator-side check it describes.

findings.title: Hard-coded `--features=rolling-updates` replaces a user's own feature list for the command
findings.body: The macro now always ends the command with `--features=rolling-updates`. Users who already turn on other features with `--features` or `KC_FEATURES` will copy this line as written. The CLI value then wins over their configured list, so the metadata/check run uses a different feature set from the real deployment. That goes against the guide's own warning to include every configuration option (`update-compatibility.adoc:70-75`, `87-91`). It does no harm today, because the check only compares versions. It will produce wrong results once features are compared. Consider telling users to add `rolling-updates` to their existing `--features` list instead of appending a separate flag.

findings.title: Exit-code remap (recreate 4→3, new 4 = feature disabled) has no test
findings.body: This change moves `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and gives 4 a new meaning, feature disabled. The guide tells automation to rely only on these exit codes (`update-compatibility.adoc:55`). No test checks either value: `UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled` only checks the error message, and `testWrongVersions` only checks stderr text (`UpdateCommandDistTest.java:48-50`, `96-106`). Adding `assertEquals(4, ...)` and `assertEquals(3, result.exitCode())` would stop the codes from drifting away from the documented table, which is how 4 and 3 got mixed up before this PR.

contracts.action: update-compatibility check/metadata now refuse to run unless the rolling-updates feature is enabled
contracts.equivalent_path: The same command's normal end: print the result, then picocli.exit(result.exitCode())
contracts.before_after: Before: printPreviewWarning, then validateConfig, then the work. After: the feature check runs first; it prints the error and calls picocli.exit(4), then returns. The return matters because Picocli.exit does not call System.exit in test launch mode.
contracts.visible_effect: stderr shows "Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled." and the process exits with 4.
contracts.failure_mode: None beyond the intended refusal. The UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46-50 path is identical.

contracts.action: Recreate exit code changed 4→3; 4 now means feature disabled
contracts.before_after: The code now matches the documented table (3 = recreate, 4 = feature disabled).
contracts.visible_effect: The check command's process exit code, which scripts consume
contracts.failure_mode: No Operator code reads these exit codes, so the remap affects only external scripts.

contracts.action: Operator docs/test enable the rolling-updates feature in the Keycloak CR
contracts.before_after: The feature reaches the server only as a --features option. No Operator logic is gated on it.
contracts.visible_effect: None in Operator behaviour. The docs claim the Operator fails without it, which is not true.

summary: The PR adds a preview `rolling-updates` feature and makes the `update-compatibility` commands require it. It also fixes the recreate exit code so the code matches the documented 3 and gives 4 the meaning "feature disabled". The code changes look correct. Three non-blocking points: the Operator guide says the Operator will fail without the feature, but no Operator code checks it. The docs macro hard-codes `--features=rolling-updates`, which overrides a user's own feature list. No test checks the remapped exit codes.
